sources.entry: Langfuse - LLM engineering platform for model tracing, prompt management, and application evaluation. Langfuse helps teams collaboratively debug, analyze, and iterate on their LLM applications such as chatbots or AI agents. (Demo, Source Code, Clients) MIT Docker

summary.one_liner: Langfuse is an open source LLM engineering platform for tracing, prompt management, evaluation, and debugging of LLM applications such as chatbots and AI agents.
summary.what_it_does: Langfuse records LLM calls and other application logic (retrieval, embedding, agent actions) as traces, letting teams inspect logs and user sessions. It provides centralized prompt management with versioning and server/client caching, and a playground for testing prompts and model configurations. Evaluation support includes LLM-as-a-judge, code evaluators, user feedback, manual labeling, and custom pipelines via APIs/SDKs. Datasets can be used for test sets, benchmarks, and experiments, with integrations for LangChain and LlamaIndex. A public API, OpenAPI spec, Postman collection, and typed Python and JS/TS SDKs are provided. The README says it can be self-hosted with Docker Compose, on a VM, or on Kubernetes via Helm.
use_cases: trace and debug LLM application calls
evaluate LLM outputs with LLM-as-a-judge or manual labeling
build test sets and benchmarks for LLM apps
iterate on prompts in a playground
notable: Integrations with OpenAI SDK, LangChain, LlamaIndex, Haystack, LiteLLM, Vercel AI SDK, and Mastra
OpenTelemetry-free @observe() Python decorator and drop-in OpenAI wrapper for quick instrumentation
Self-hosting options: Docker Compose, VM, Helm, and Terraform templates for AWS, Azure, GCP
Prompt caching on server and client side to avoid added latency
Telemetry can be disabled with TELEMETRY_ENABLED=false
caveats: Licensed MIT except the 'ee' folders, which have separate terms
Self-hosted production deployment is recommended on Kubernetes via Helm, which implies more setup than the Docker Compose quickstart
By default self-hosted instances send basic usage statistics to PostHog unless opted out
